messages:
alicia (sales): Hey team, Acme's POC is hitting intermittent 429s during bulk embedding runs this morning. They run ~8 concurrent batches (batch_size=128) against /v1/embeddings and it spikes around 09:10-09:20 PST. Can we triage?

nina (solutions): Do we have their request headers / a sample curl? Also which plan/dedicated vs hosted?

alicia (sales): Hosted (trial account). Sample curl + response below from the customer: 

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-POC123" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1024","input":[...]}'
```

Response headers: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 2
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 164
Request-Id: r-84f3a2
```

mike (eng-oncall): Thanks — that Request-Id is helpful. A few quick checks: are they reusing the same API key across parallel workers? If so the per-key burst may be exhausted even if overall account allotment exists. Also which route they call exactly (/v1/embeddings) matters because we have per-route caps.

alicia (sales): They spawn 8 workers each with the same key; each worker sends 7 req/s for ~30s bursts.

jamal (eng-sre): That pattern explains it. Hosted trial keys have a short burst window (60s) and a per-route concurrency cap — for embeddings route we cap sustained requests at ~100 req/min for trials with a burst multiplier of 3. If 8 workers align bursts you'll see immediate 429s and Retry-After.

jamal (eng-sre): Also note token-based budgeting: large batch_size=128 => bigger token footprint per call, so token budget can be reached before request-count cap depending on how throttles are configured.

sophia (eng-infra): Can you pull the server-side trace for Request-Id r-84f3a2 and paste the internal throttle tags? If they hit "route_cap::embeddings_v1" + "burst_window_exhausted" that's the root cause.

alicia (sales): Pasting truncated server trace the customer supplied from their headers and our support logs: 
```
[ingress] request-id=r-84f3a2 route=/v1/embeddings key=sk-POC123 tokens=5120 status=429 throttle=route_cap:embeddings_v1 burst_window_exhausted
```

mike (eng-oncall): Yep — confirmed. Two mitigation paths: (1) client-side: throttle to a lower concurrency and add jitter/exponential backoff on 429s (use Retry-After header). Recommend spreading workers or using a local rate limiter like token-bucket. (2) short-term ops: we can bump the trial per-route burst 2x for a 1-hour window so Acme can finish their demo.

nina (solutions): What about long-term for POC? They need predictable throughput for embeddings. Can we propose a Dedicated trial or explicit per-route quota in Sales offer?

jamal (eng-sre): For POC we usually do a temporary quota bump + guidance to instrument X-RateLimit headers and switch to per-tenant key per worker. For Dedicated, we provide reserved capacity and configurable burst windows so this won't happen.

alicia (sales): Customer asked about pricing impact if we increase quota. What's the quick answer?

sophia (eng-infra): Increase will be billable at normal rates; for short trial we typically offer a credits offset. I'll flag pricing with GTM but ops needs explicit approval to change runtime caps.

mike (eng-oncall): Action items:
- @sophia to approve 1-hour per-route bump for sk-POC123 (ops ticket)
- @jamal to monitor for collateral impact (any noisy neighbors)
- @nina to update Acme with client-side throttling guidance + suggested config (reduce batch_size to 64 or add 200ms jitter)
- @alicia to get final approval from customer for demo window

rate-limiter-bot: Ticket #INC-2023 created to track the quota-bump request (ops ticket link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2023) :white_check_mark:

alicia (sales): I'll coordinate with the customer now and confirm when they're ready. Thanks everyone — seems like we can unblock with a short bump and config changes. :thumbsup:
